The key variable in the near term is how quickly new Permian processing and fractionation projects fill with volumes that support the higher 2026 and 2027 growth capex plans.

The main operational risk right now is execution on that spend and keeping complex assets running smoothly. Any repeat of PDH unit reliability issues or weaker demand for LPG exports, where management has already flagged near term overcapacity, would pressure returns on recent investments. The latest valuation debate does not materially change those core business drivers.

Enterprise Products Partners has raised growth capex to roughly US$2.9b to US$3.4b for 2026, with about US$3b flagged for 2027, largely tied to new Permian plants, NGL pipelines and fractionation.
